title: Agentic Unlearning: When LLM Agent Meets Machine Unlearning

object.carrier: Five-layer external memory store (episodic dialogue traces M, semantic summaries S, reflections R, procedural and external layers) organized as a dependency graph G=(V,E) with per-node reference counters and a persistent blocklist B; prototype store holds 2000 entries encoded by text-embedding-ada-002 (1536-dim), hybrid retrieval top-5 (semantic weight 0.7, keyword 0.3); deletion targets plus their dependency closure are pruned, vector index rebuilt when |B| > tau=100

safety_property.statement: Verifiable removal of targeted information from BOTH parametric and memory pathways of a memory-augmented agent without utility loss on retained data, preventing parameter-memory backflow: (i) the agent does not reveal target information D_tgt under adaptive interaction; (ii) memory contains no artifacts derived from D_tgt; (iii) the agent cannot rewrite D_tgt back into memory; (iv) utility on retained data is preserved. Failure condition: the backflow recontamination loop - parametric residue regenerates forgotten content which is re-stored, or residual memory artifacts re-expose deleted content through retrieval.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Forget-set accuracy (lower = better removal), Test-set accuracy and held-out generalization accuracy (utility preservation), MIA AUC (ideal 0.5) and normalized MIA Score on member vs non-member loss distributions, memory-side forget/retain accuracy before vs after unlearning (Table 4), and Agent-Loop retrieval hit rate across Store/Query/Delete/Probe stages (Figure 6); forget set sizes Q_F=100 and Q_F=1000; mean±std over 3 runs.

capabilities: Membership-inference attacker: computes area under the ROC curve from loss distributions of member vs non-member data to detect whether forgotten records remain distinguishable (MIA AUC near 1 = under-unlearning, near 0 = over-unlearning)
assumptions: Deletion requests arrive incrementally as forget sets D_F over medical QA data; retain set D_R is available for the utility-preserving loss term
Memory is modeled as a dependency graph over {M,S,R,K}; unlearning guarantees depend on the graph structure, not on specific memory-layer content
Retrieval honors the blocklist at retrieval boundaries (Invariant 1: no memory in B appears in results); derived artifacts follow dependency consistency (Invariant 2)
not_covered: No adaptive multi-turn attacker in the evaluation: property (i) (no revelation under adaptive interaction) is defined but the measured attacks are static forget-set accuracy, MIA, and a scripted four-stage agent loop, not an adaptive red-team
Dependency tracking may not fully capture cross-agent information flow in shared knowledge graphs (authors' stated limitation; multi-agent unlearning left to future work)
Deployment in clinical settings and formal HIPAA/GDPR compliance verification are out of scope (Ethical Statement)

intervention.name: Synchronized Backflow Unlearning (SBU): dual-pathway agentic unlearning
intervention.description: Memory pathway: dependency-aware unlearning - target IDs are added to a persistent blocklist for O(1) retrieval filtering, the dependency closure Dep(D_F) is traversed with reference counting to mark exclusively-dependent artifacts for deletion while preserving shared ones, zero-reference nodes are batch-removed, targets and their vectors are deleted, and the vector index is rebuilt when |B|>100; all operations logged in a tamper-evident write-ahead log with hash-chain verification. Parameter pathway: entropy-regularized unlearning (KL-to-random) - a frozen randomly-initialized reference model defines a high-entropy prior; the objective L_weight = L_CE^{D_R} + lambda_F T^2 L_KL^{D_F} aligns outputs on forget queries to the random-like distribution while cross-entropy on retain queries preserves utility. Unified protocol: memory unlearning executes FIRST so parameter updates operate on a sanitized retrieval context, preventing re-encoding; the process repeats per incremental request.

results.claim: On MedQA (Q_F=100), SBU achieves MIA Score 0.895 - a 24.8% improvement in privacy protection over baselines whose scores stagnate near the Original model (0.727) - while maintaining test accuracy 92.50% and generalization 90.50%.
results.metric: MIA Score (higher better) with test/gen accuracy (%)
results.comparison: Sequential LoRA MIA 0.717 / test 88.67; Sequential Retrain 0.729; GA 0.764; NPO 0.727; Adapter Merging 0.729; Origin 0.727
results.setting: II-Medical-8B (Qwen3-8B based) with external memory (2000 entries, top-5 hybrid retrieval), MedQA forget set Q_F=100, mean±std over 3 runs (Table 2)
results.quote: In contrast, SBU achieves a MIA Score of 0.895, representing a 24.8% improvement in privacy protection, while maintaining test accuracy (92.50%) and generalization (90.50%).

denominator.how_counted: Forget set size Q_F=100 MedQA questions; metrics reported as mean±std over 3 runs; test accuracy over the MedQA test split

results.claim: Memory-side forgetting: on MedQA (Q_F=100), memory accuracy on the forget set drops from 78% to 14% after memory unlearning while retain-set memory accuracy slightly rises from 54% to 56%.
results.metric: memory retrieval accuracy (%) on forget vs retain sets
results.comparison: before vs after memory unlearning (Table 4); MedMCQA forget 84% -> 30%, MedReason forget 68% -> 26%
results.setting: External memory system of II-Medical-8B, Q_F=100, memory-side pathway evaluation (Table 4)
results.quote: As shown in Table 4, for MedQA with QF=100, the memory accuracy on the forget set drops from 78% to 14% after unlearning, while the memory accuracy on the retain set slightly increases from 54% to 56%.

denominator.how_counted: Memory accuracy = fraction of forget/retain queries whose answers are correctly served from the memory store, before vs after unlearning; absolute query counts per set not stated

results.claim: Agent-Loop evaluation (Store, Query, Delete, Probe): after the deletion request at T4, forget-set retrieval hit rate falls from 100% to 0% while the retain set remains accessible, and summary updates plus dependency cleanup prevent indirect leakage through derived content.
results.metric: retrieval hit rate (%) in a four-stage interactive agent loop
results.comparison: pre-deletion vs post-deletion probes within the interactive loop
results.setting: Agent Loop with stages Store (T1-T2), Query (T3), Delete (T4), Probe (T5-T6) on medical Q&A pairs (Figure 6b)
results.quote: As shown in Figure 6(b), the Forget Set retrieval hit rate drops from 100% to 0% while the Retain Set remains accessible.

denominator.how_counted: Hit rate over probe queries issued against the memory store before and after the deletion request; number of probe queries not stated

results.claim: Pathway ablation: removing the memory pathway (w/o Mem) degrades MIA-based privacy (MIA Score 0.834 vs 0.895 full), and the Mem-Only variant underperforms on forget (85.67) and test (88.33) accuracy - the two pathways are complementary.
results.comparison: full SBU vs w/o Mem vs Mem-Only (Table 6)
results.quote: As shown in Table 6, removing the memory pathway leads to a noticeable degradation in MIA-based privacy metrics. In contrast, the Mem-Only variant underperforms on forget and test set accuracies, despite some privacy improvement.

denominator.how_counted: Same MedQA Q_F=100 evaluation protocol as Table 2; per-variant item counts identical to the main setup

results.claim: Scalability: at Q_F=1000 on MedMCQA, SBU reaches MIA Score 0.996 (MIA AUC 0.5000, i.e., at the ideal) with forget accuracy 71.33 and test 89.33, while baseline privacy metrics stagnate around MIA Score ≈0.62 at Q_F=1000 on MedQA.
results.metric: MIA Score (higher better), forget set size 1000
results.comparison: baselines ≈0.62 (MedQA Q_F=1000, Supplementary Table 1); Retraining Oracle 0.9920; Naive Deletion 0.9067; Re-indexing 0.9640 (Table 5)
results.setting: MedMCQA forget set Q_F=1000, mean±std over 3 runs (Table 3)
results.quote: On MedMCQA (QF=1000, Table 3), SBU reaches a MIA Score of 0.996.

denominator.how_counted: Forget set size Q_F=1000 MedMCQA questions; mean±std over 3 runs

results.claim: Cost reading (tuning trade-off): the forgetting coefficient has a narrow safe range - lambda_F below 0.5 fails to induce sufficient forgetting (forget accuracy 86%), lambda_F >= 3.0 causes test degradation to 66%, and temperature T=4.0 destabilizes optimization and drops test accuracy to 68%.
results.metric: forget vs test accuracy (%) across 34 hyperparameter configurations
results.value: test 66% at lambda_F>=3.0; test 68% at T=4.0
results.comparison: optimal configuration (lambda_F=1.5, T=2.0, entropy fallback): 90% test with forget 68%
results.setting: 34 configurations on MedMCQA varying lambda_F, temperature T, and entropy fallback (Figure 5)
results.quote: The forgetting coefficient λF\lambda_{F} controls forgetting-utility trade-off: values below 0.5 fail to induce sufficient forgetting (forget accuracy 86%); excessive values (λF≥3.0\lambda_{F}{\geq}3.0) cause test degradation (66%) despite stronger forgetting (forget accuracy 64%). Temperature exhibits a narrow effective range, with moderate values (1.0–2.0) performing best, whereas high temperature (T=4.0T{=}4.0) destabilizes optimization and drops test accuracy to 68%.

denominator.how_counted: 34 hyperparameter configurations evaluated on MedMCQA; accuracy per configuration

limitations.statement: Dependency tracking does not capture cross-agent information flow in shared knowledge graphs; multi-agent unlearning protocols are deferred to future work.
limitations.quote: A limitation of our current approach is that dependency tracking may not fully capture cross-agent information flow in shared knowledge graphs. Future work will explore unlearning protocols specifically tailored for multi-agent collaborative environments.

limitations.statement: The blocklist-based design leaves vector-index staleness that must be managed by periodic rebuilds (threshold tau=100), i.e., deletion is only eventually consistent at the index level.
limitations.quote: To control vector-index staleness, the system periodically rebuilds the vector index when |B| exceeds threshold τ=100\tau=100.

limitations.statement: The entropy-alignment design deliberately avoids a perfectly uniform output distribution because that risks over-unlearning and capability damage; the KL-to-random scheme is chosen for stability.
limitations.quote: However, our KL-to-random scheme provides a more stable learning target by aligning to a structured high-entropy prior from a reference model, rather than forcing the output towards a perfectly uniform distribution, which can risk over-unlearning and damaging model capabilities.

counterexamples.observation: NPO attains the lowest forget accuracy (74.00%) but suffers severe generalization collapse (gen 41.67%) - aggressive forgetting destroys retained capability, demonstrating that parameter-only aggressive unlearning is not a viable cost profile.

reproduction.data: MedQA (~10k questions), MedMCQA (~183k questions, 2,400 topics, 21 subjects), MedReason (~33k QA pairs, answer pairs only); forget sets Q_F=100 and Q_F=1000; memory store 2000 entries; 3 runs per configuration
